Funny thing about “failed systems”…

Washington only calls something broken after they’ve spent years ignoring the warnings that would’ve prevented the mess in the first place.

Here’s what never gets mentioned:

• From 2017–2024, GAO repeatedly told Congress that premium spikes were driven by their own decisions underfunded risk pools, unstable marketplace rules, and year to year subsidy cliffs that made insurers price defensively.

• In 2020, the Treasury Inspector General warned that IRS lacked the tools to validate premium-tax-credit eligibility in real time, yet Congress never passed the reforms that both parties agreed were needed.

• And in 2025, the House cut funding for CMS program integrity staff the same analysts tasked with stopping the fraud today’s talking points blame on everyone but Congress.

So yes, fixing the system matters.

But no amount of speeches about “$400 billion” changes the fact that Congress created most of these problems by refusing to modernize verification, stabilize the rules, or enforce the oversight they already had.
